correctness.rationale: The four-dimensional exact equitable compression is obtained from explicit clique eigenvectors. The two low frequencies are separated from the high frequencies by a gap of order the smaller clique size. Resolvent substitution bounds eigenvalue and low-eigenvector corrections by order inverse-size squared, and high components by order inverse-size to the three-halves. Two Duhamel estimates bound the residual high-high amplitude. This yields the claimed uniform bounded-time amplitude formula. Squaring at the fixed half-period gives the exact leading infidelity. At unequal finite orders the squared adjacency moments are distinct, ruling out even arbitrarily good state transfer. Full-to-reduced and block-coordinate calculations were checked in the package. There is no unproved extrapolation from numerical data.

value.rationale: The physical distinction is substantive: a one-edge bottleneck between two irregularly sized dense quantum networks permits near-unit transfer after a size-independent waiting time; even though for each finite size mismatch, perfect and pretty-good transfer are both impossible. The leading failure probability separates as the inverse of each clique order, giving a concrete size–fidelity design rule and a scale-sensitive boundary between finite and growing networks, not merely a numerical gain or relabeling.
